Resolve every join key pair's common type

Source: R/join.R
resolve_join_key_types.Rd

Schema-only (no GPU work). dplyr casts each key pair to its common type (vctrs::vec_ptype2()) before matching and errors when a pair has none; the ladder is resolve_common_col_type() (R/bind.R), shared with bind_rows() and the set operations. Walks equi AND non-equi pairs so an incompatible pair raises at verb time, in eager and lazy mode.

Usage

resolve_join_key_types(
  x_schema,
  y_schema,
  join_spec,
  x_unspecified = NULL,
  y_unspecified = NULL
)

Arguments

x_schema, y_schema

Schemas of the two inputs

join_spec

A join spec from parse_join_by()

x_unspecified, y_unspecified

Names of each side's vctrs::unspecified() columns (the tbls' $unspecified)

Value

join_spec, with key_casts set when any equi pair needs a cast (and key_abort, see above)

Details

Pairs whose types already match (the common, benchmarked case) cost one vector comparison and leave join_spec untouched. Equi pairs with compatible-but-different types are recorded in join_spec$key_casts: idx (position in the spec), type (the common type), cast_left/ cast_right, the source types, and a factor side's levels (needed to decode it to STRING). Non-equi numeric pairs are only validated (the expression evaluator widens their operands itself); a rolling INT32/FLOAT64 pair is recorded (it is searched, not evaluated) and so is a non-equi STRING pair (string_codes = TRUE, see below).

A BOOL8 key against a STRING, factor, Date or POSIXct key is not an error here: dplyr (vctrs) gives an all-NA logical the other side's type, but only the data can say whether the column is one. Such a pair is recorded with unspecified = TRUE; apply_join_key_casts() checks the values when the join runs and raises the incompatible-type error then. A verb that records one without marker computes the join at once (a plan break in lazy mode, see join_key_check_reads_data()), so dplyr's error is raised at the verb. marker is TRUE for a vctrs::unspecified() column (named in the tbl's $unspecified): known all-NA, no data check.

A pair that has no common type and comes after such an unchecked pair is not raised at once: dplyr names the first bad pair in by order, and the earlier one is only known from the data. The resolver stores it as join_spec$key_abort (the arguments of the error) and stops; the join raises it after the earlier pairs' checks.

lower_join() applies the plan; build_join_output_info() reads it for the merged key's output type.
